expected.sentence:

Verdict as recorded: Guilty of assault with a deadly weapon; acquitted of attempted murder (after two prior hung juries); conviction later reversed on grand-jury-composition grounds (In re Wells, 1971)

Charges as recorded: Two counts of attempted murder and two counts of assault with a deadly weapon against Oakland police officers, arising from the April 6, 1968 West Oakland gun battle

updates.sentence: Indeterminate term of one to fifteen years after conviction of assault with a deadly weapon and acquittal of attempted murder. On October 18, 1971 the appellate court reversed with directions for a hearing on the grand-jury challenge; it did not order unconditional release. Actual release date remains unverified.

expected.sentence:
Six months; served 44 days at the Santa Rita Prison Farm before Supreme Court Justice William O. Douglas granted a stay of sentence

Charges as recorded: Misdemeanor stemming from the May 2, 1967 armed Black Panther protest at the California State Capitol in Sacramento (disrupting the legislative session); arrested alongside Huey Newton and Bobby Seale

updates.sentence: Case arising from the May 2, 1967 Sacramento Capitol protest. An individual sentence and time served for this case have not been verified; the documented forty-four-day stay at Santa Rita preceded this protest and belongs to the separate Oakland Tribune case.

entries.rationale: Remove misplaced six-month sentence and forty-four-day narrative from the 1967 case: the December 1966 newspaper proves that stay occurred earlier. No biography changes.
